Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second innings. Indian players have made their way out in the middle. Najmul Hossain Shanto and Zakir Hasan are the openers for Bangladesh. Mohammed Siraj to start the proceedings with the ball. Here we go.
... Second Innings ...

India have managed to cross the 400-run mark! After a shaky start to the first session, the duo of Kuldeep Yadav and Ashwin posted a 92-run stand. From 293/7 they went on to 385 runs and lost Ashwin after that but the damage was done. Kuldeep Yadav was dismissed soon after that and Umesh Yadav delivered a cameo of 15 runs off 10 deliveries. The pick of the bowlers for Bangladesh were Mehidy Hasan and Taijul Islam as they took four wickets each whilst Khaled Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain took one each. Earlier, it was the 149-run stand between Iyer and Pujara that brought India to a healthy position after losing four wickets early. Both missed out on their centuries but did their job and as mentioned before the duo of Taijul Islam and Mehidy Hasan did the bulk of the work for Bangladesh. The pitch is not easy to bat on and Indian spinners will fancy their chances here. Stay tuned as Bangladesh will be ready with their reply in a short while.

…Day 2, Session 2…

Bangladesh bowlers started well and it was Ebadot Hossain who got Iyer at the start. They did bowl well after that and had some instances where they did trouble Ashwin and Kuldeep Yadav but missed on getting a breakthrough. Shakib will be happy with how the bowlers performed but would have hoped to wrap up things quickly after the wicket of Iyer early in the session. They now will be looking to bag early wickets at the start of the second session and bundle out the opponents quickly. Can they do it soon? Or will India keep their scoreboard ticking? We shall find out shortly. Do join us at 11.40 am IST (6:10 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 30 overs, 70 runs, and 1 wicket. India had a shaky start in this session as Iyer who resumed the day at 82 was dismissed soon after he added 4 runs to his score. Bangladesh had the momentum with them early in the session as they had restricted the runs and picked up a wicket at the start but Ashwin and Kuldeep Yadav came up with a gritty partnership of 55 runs and kept the scoreboard ticking. The session started at 278/6 and India is now playing at 348/7. Kuldeep Yadav is on 21 whilst Ashwin is playing on 40.

We are all ready for the start of Day 2! The Bangladesh players are out there in the middle while Shreyas Iyer, the overnight Indian batter is joined by Ravichandran Ashwin who is a new batter after a wicket on the last delivery of Day 1. Spin to start and it will be Taijul Islam with the ball first up. Here we go...

Cheteshwar Pujara is down for a quick chat. He says that he is happy with the way he batted and had couple of important partnerships first with Pant and then with Iyer. He says that he would have liked to get a hundred but overall is happy with his performance as at one time getting to 250 was also looking tough. Mentions that it is bit difficult to bat with a hard ball but it gets easy with a softer ball. Feels that as a batter you are never in on this surface and there is one ball in every over that can get one out. Tells that if they can reach 350 there will be nothing like it but adds that anything over 300 will be good. He also feels that seamers will also have a role to play on this pitch.

Anjum Chopra is down for the Pitch Report. She says that everyone thought at the start of the Day 1 that it will be a good pitch to bat on and it is but adds that there is bit turn and bounce too. Mentions that there are few marks and abrasiveness in the surface but it is bound to happen when the pitch is 90 overs old. Feels that it creates doubts in the mind of the batters and says that from the batter's point of vew playing on the front foot on this pitch will be a safer option.

Shakib Al Hasan would be slightly unhappy as they let India off the hook after taking three wickets in the first session. Taijul Islam and Mehidy Hasan did strike late in the day to even things out a bit but missed a few chances in the middle and final season which can prove them costly eventually.  They will be hoping to bag some quick wickets in the opening session now and bundle India to a par total. Can they do it? Or will India come up with something special and post a mammoth total on the board? An important first session of Day 2 coming up.

After deciding to bat first, India started steadily as the openers KL Rahul, and Shubman Gill added 41 runs for the first wicket. After losing Gill, the wickets kept on tumbling for them until Rishabh Pant and Cheteshwar Pujara steadied the ship for a while. Pant was dismissed for a quickfire 46 and after that, Shreyas Iyer and Pujara brewed a mammoth 149-run partnership. Pujara was however dismissed but Iyer is unbeaten on 82 and India would be hoping that Ravichandran Ashwin and Iyer can stitch a big partnership here.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 2 of the first Test match between Bangladesh and India. The game looks evenly poised as of now, courtesy of two wickets late in Day 1 for Bangladesh after an excellent partnership between Shreyas Iyer and Cheteshwar Pujara. The scoreboard reads 278/6 as of now and India will be looking to extend the score to around 400 while Bangladesh will be looking to bag some quick wickets in the morning session.
…Day 2, Session 1…

Right then, that is it from the Day 1 of this first Test match. Bangladesh have done themselves a world of good by picking those two late wickets in the day but they now need to comeback stronger on Day 2 and restrict India to as low a total as possible as the pitch is certainly not easy to bat. Can they do it? Or will India come up with something special? We shall find out on Thursday, 15th of December at 9 am IST (3:30 am GMT). Do join us a bit early for the build-up as well. Till then, goodbye and cheers!

Earlier in the day, India began slowly after opting to bat first. At 41 they lost Gill and then the wickets kept on tumbling for them. They were soon 48/3 when Pant and Pujara steadied the sinking ship. India needed to get a move on to reach a good total, but soon when a good partnership was brewing, they lost Pant in the second session. The pair of Pujara and Iyer provided a much-needed impetus and kept the scoreboard ticking for them.

Pujara and Iyer brewed a 149-run partnership when their team needed them the most. Pujara was dismissed at 90 but Iyer kept on going and was joined by Axar Patel. However, Axar Patel lost his wicket on the last ball of the day as well. Have to mention a lifeline that Iyer got, a rare moment where the ball kissed the stumps but the bails did not come off. Ebadot Hossain also dropped a sitter and Iyer lived a charmed life but made full use of it in the end. KL Rahul will be pleased with the day's disciplined batting effort after a poor start and they would be looking to get to around 400 on Day 2.

Bangladesh will be pleased with how things ended for them and their bowlers tried very hard and kept their discipline throughout the day. Taijul Islam set the tone for Bangladesh with two wickets at the start alongside Khaled Ahmed and Mehidy Hasan taking one. After the dismissal of Pant, the Bangladesh bowlers just couldn't break the Pujara-Iyer stubborn partnership. However, Taijul Islam again came back to Bangladesh's rescue again and got Pujara at the end of the third session and then Mehidy Hasan got Axar Patel on the last ball of the day to make things pretty even at the end of Day 1.

Bangladesh have done really well to put India under pressure in this decent batting deck. Taijul Islam bagged two whilst Mehidy Hasan and Khaled Ahmed took one each. They are now trying hard to break this Pujara-Iyer partnership but they will have to come up with something special here. Shakib Al Hasan will want to break this stubborn partnership soon. Can he do it? Or will these two batters continue to bat freely? We will find out shortly. Do join us at 2 pm IST (8.30 am GMT) post tea break.

SESSION SUMMARY - 30 overs, 89 runs and 1 wicket. India started off slowly in the opening session and lost Gill early on in the game. Soon after they were 41/1, they lost wickets in a jiffy and were 48/3. Pant and Pujara played a gritty stand but Pant was dismissed on 112. After the wicket of Rishabh Pant, India have slowed down a touch and batted cautiously. Pujara went on batting in his own usual style while Iyer looked to settle in with him. They are now looking solid and made India reach 174. Pujara is playing on 42 while Iyer is on 41.

India, on the other hand, after the start they got would not have expected to lose three wickets in this session. Both Shubman Gill and KL Rahul looked pretty comfortable in the middle before a miscalculated shot from Gill brought his downfall. The big guns, Rahul and Kohli followed soon and from 41-0, India were reduced to 48-3. However, Pant with his little counterattacking knock has provided some respite for India but they need the pair of Pujara and Pant to bat long now. It promises to be an enticing second session of this Test match and we will be back at 11.40 am IST (6.10 am GMT). Stay tuned.

A productive first session for Bangladesh! They have managed to pick three wickets in the session and have shown a lot of discipline and grit that is required in Test cricket. Taijul Islam delivered a beautiful spell as he usually does in Bangladesh and made things happen after Indian openers got off to a confident start. He got Gill first up and was ably supported by Khaled Ahmed who also bowled brilliantly in his second spell to get rid of the Indian skipper, KL Rahul. However, it was the wicket of Virat Kohli that has put Bangladesh right on top here and they would be looking to build on this momentum now.

We are moments away from the start of this first Test match! Bangladesh players have made their way out to the middle and it is a bright and sunny morning here in Chattogram. The Indian openers, KL Rahul and Shubman Gill also make their way out to the middle now. There might be some help for the seamers early on and we have Ebadot Hossain to start the proceedings with the ball. Three slips and a gully in position. KL Rahul is on the strike. Here we go...

Mohammed Siraj is down for a quick chat. He says that Test cricket is his favourite format and tells that he loves Test cricket. He mentions that he prepares well for this format. Feels that he is playing well and adds that the ODI series went well for him and that gives him some more confidence coming into this Test series.

Shakib Al Hasan, the skipper of Bangladesh says that they would have batted first and tells that it looks like a good wicket. Mentions that history says more wickets fall on the first day than the last day and hopes to take early wickets and put pressure on India. Informs that they will play Test cricket after five months and it is a bit difficult to adjust but feels that they have prepared well. Says that they have not got the results they wanted in Test cricket but hopes to do well and get some World Test Championship points. Informs that they are playing two seamers and three spinners.

KL Rahul, the skipper of India says that they will bat first as it's a good wicket and try and put more runs on board and play well. Adds that they have lost Rohit Sharma and some guys due to injuries but it gives chance to the new guys and they will be happy to contribute to the team. Ends by saying that Kuldeep Yadav is playing alongside Ravichandran Ashwin and Axar Patel and the two pacers are Umesh Yadav and Mohammed Siraj.

India (Playing XI) - KL Rahul (C), Shubman Gill, Cheteshwar Pujara, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Rishabh Pant (WK), Ravichandran Ashwin, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Umesh Yadav, Mohammed Siraj.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of KL Rahul. India have elected to BAT first.
Zakir Hasan is seen receiving his maiden Test cap in the Bangladesh team huddle from the skipper Shakib Al Hasan. A big moment for the young man as he is all set to make his Test debut!

PITCH REPORT -  Sanjay Manjrekar is down for the Pitch Report. He says that he is surprised the look of the pitch. Tells that there is a decent covering of grass but adds that it is there to ensure that cracks does not bigger and wider over the course of five days, Tells that the pitch is hard and adds that India will play seamers but reckons that there is enough roughness for the spinners to work with. Informs that captain winning the toss will want to bat first.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, have not been able to make much of an impact in the longest format of the game. They are missing the services of the experienced Tamim Iqbal and they need to find runs from their top order to compete in this game. Skipper, Shakib Al Hasan will lead the bowling attack with Mehidy Hasan, Taijul Islam forming a formidable spin trio while Ebadot Hossain will need to play a key role in pace department. The stakes are high and both sides will look forward to a win this game. Which side will come out on top? Let's find out. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

India last played a Test in July this year against England and it might take some time for KL Rahul and his boys to make the transition to the 5-day format in the absence of senior players like Rohit Sharma, Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Shami. Virat Kohli though will be eager to take the guard in the middle to keep his form running. The pace trio of Umesh Yadav, Mohammed Siraj and Shardul Thakur is most likely to get the cut but it would be interesting to see the composition of India’s bowling attack here in Chattogram with some quality spinners in the ranks as well.

Hello and a warm welcome at Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium, Chattogram as Bangladesh and India get ready to lock horns against each other in the first Test of this two-match Test series. Bangladesh won the ODI series against India and it will definitely boost their confidence coming into this Test series. The Indian team, on the other hand, will look forward to keeping their unbeaten record against Bangladesh in the Tests and boost their chances of making it to the World Test Championship final.
